Ignore black bars around the picture (works for 16:9, 1.85:1, 2.39:1 content). Off by default.

Camera capture receives no standby signal from the TV, so a powered-off screen keeps streaming sensor noise to the strip. When enabled, the LEDs turn off once the picture goes blank, and frame transmission pauses until the picture returns. Disabled by default.

When enabled, frame transmission also pauses if the picture stops changing (e.g. a paused video or a static menu); the strip retains its last displayed colors. Disabled by default, as an extended static scene will freeze the strip\'s colors.

Before using this app, you need to set up your LED controller:

• WLED: Configure WLED firmware on your ESP8266/ESP32 device
• Adalight: Connect Arduino with Adalight firmware via USB
• Hyperion: Install and configure Hyperion server

For detailed setup instructions, please visit the GitHub repository.

Lets Universal Ambient Light capture the screen for the ambient lighting and press TV buttons on commands from a paired phone.
Please enable the Accessibility Service for Universal Ambient Light

This app uses the AccessibilityService API to capture screen content. This is required to analyze colors on your screen and sync them with your background lights (Ambilight) in real-time.

The screen data is processed locally on your device, is never saved, and is never transmitted to any third-party servers.

If you do not agree, you cannot use this capture mode.

Uses ADB once to allow screen capture without a confirmation dialog, windows over other apps and unrestricted background work. Without them Android 10+ cannot bring the lighting back by itself after the TV wakes up or reboots. The phone films the TV and the glow on the wall and compares when the picture and the strip change. The delay is measured on what is playing right now, so every app and source gets its own value.

Per-app delay and auto-tuning with the phone camera
If the strip runs ahead of the picture, a delay holds it back. Players and sources process video differently, so an app can have its own delay: the TV switches to it while that app is on screen.
The phone camera films the TV and the glow and finds the delay on the movie that is playing.
Auto-tuning runs from a phone: open TV remote on it, connect to this TV and go to Settings, Lighting delay.
The TV does not report which app is on screen. Grant usage access via ADB, otherwise the delay for all apps is used everywhere.
